title_en: Supreme People's Court Publishes Four Typical Drug Crime Cases
keywords_en: drugs; four typical cases of drug crimes published
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Releases Four Typical Drug Crime Cases

This year marks the furtherance of the new round of anti-drug efforts. To enhance the People's Courts' comprehensive drug control work this year, the Supreme People's Court has adopted multiple measures. In March, the Supreme People's Court issued a notice to the Higher People's Courts of 16 regions with a high incidence of drug cases, requiring them to concentrate anti-drug publicity activities in April, June, and September respectively, to form a momentum for the People's Courts to severely crack down on serious drug crimes in accordance with the law. In April, the Supreme People's Court also released five typical drug crime cases where the death penalty was approved. On April 12, the Supreme People's Court issued the "Notice on Conscientiously Doing a Good Job in the People's Courts' Comprehensive Drug Control Work in 2010," requiring People's Courts at all levels, while properly handling drug crime trials, to conduct in-depth research on drug cases, further strengthen trial guidance, focus on anti-drug publicity and education, and continuously deepen the comprehensive drug control work. On the eve of the "6.26" International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking, the Supreme People's Court held a press conference to introduce the work of the People's Courts on drug control since last year and released four typical drug crime cases where the death penalty was approved.

To thoroughly implement the criminal policy of combining leniency with severity, fully leverage the role of punishment in curbing drug crimes, and reflect the principled stance of the People's Courts in severely punishing serious drug crimes in accordance with the law, the Supreme People's Court today releases another four typical drug crime cases where the death penalty was recently approved. The specific facts of the cases are as follows:

1. The Case of Defendants Chen Weidong et al. for Drug Trafficking and Transportation

In mid-May 2008, defendant Chen Weidong and Liu Weizhong drove to Shantou City, Guangdong Province. Defendant Wang Nongli took Chen Weidong to Jiazi Town, Lufeng City to purchase drugs before returning to Shantou. Subsequently, Chen Weidong and Liu Weizhong drove the drugs back to Shanghai for sale. After the case was uncovered, public security personnel seized 5,717.16 grams of methamphetamine, 11.22 grams of ketamine, 3.15 grams of caffeine, 0.64 grams of cannabis, and 0.18 grams of nimetazepam from a villa in Songjiang District, Shanghai, rented by Chen Weidong.

In early June of the same year, defendant Chen Weidong and Liu Weizhong again drove to Shantou City. Defendant Wang Nongli took the two to Jiazi Town, Lufeng City. After Chen Weidong purchased drugs, he, Liu Weizhong, and Wang Nongli carried the drugs and drove back to Shanghai for sale.

On the 20th of the same month, defendant Chen Weidong instructed defendants Liu Weizhong and Wang Nongli to carry RMB 1,000,000 in drug money to Jiazi Town, Lufeng City to hand over to drug dealers. Liu Weizhong purchased drugs and carried them back to Shanghai. At Chen Weidong's request, Liu delivered the drugs to the residence of Chen's girlfriend, Zhao Xuemin. Instructed by Chen Weidong, Zhao Xuemin sold nearly 300 grams of the methamphetamine. After the case was uncovered, public security personnel seized 987.97 grams of methamphetamine from Zhao Xuemin's residence.

On the 22nd of the same month, defendant Chen Weidong flew to Shantou City. Defendant Wang Nongli drove to pick up Chen and take him to Jiazi Town, Lufeng City. After Chen Weidong purchased drugs, he and Wang Nongli carried the drugs and returned to Shanghai by long-distance bus. At noon on the 24th, public security personnel arrested Chen Weidong and Wang Nongli on the Shanghai-Hangzhou Expressway and seized 3,545.83 grams of methamphetamine on the spot.

The court held that defendants Chen Weidong, Wang Nongli, and Liu Weizhong, for the purpose of seeking illegal profits, knowingly trafficked and transported drugs, and their actions constituted the crime of drug trafficking and transportation. Defendant Zhao Xuemin's actions constituted the crime of drug trafficking. Chen Weidong, Wang Nongli, and Liu Weizhong trafficked and transported a huge quantity of drugs, causing great social harm, and should be punished according to law. In the joint crime, Chen Weidong played an organizing and directing role and was a principal offender, and he should be punished for all crimes he organized and directed. Wang Nongli and Liu Weizhong actively participated in the drug crime and were also principal offenders, and they should be punished for all crimes in which they participated. Zhao Xuemin was an accessory and should be given a mitigated punishment according to law. Given that Liu Weizhong had major meritorious performance, his punishment could be lenient according to law. Accordingly, Chen Weidong was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved; Wang Nongli was sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve; Liu Weizhong was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of fifteen years; and Zhao Xuemin was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of eight years.

2. The Case of Defendants Ma Chongyang et al. for Drug Trafficking and Transportation

In late July 2008, defendant Ma Chongyang gave defendant Li Liang 50 grams of drugs in Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province, for sale. Li Liang brought the drugs back to Weinan City but failed to sell them. On August 18 of the same year, Ma Chongyang instructed Li Liang to return the 50 grams of drugs to Xi'an City. Ma handed the drugs to Huang Jianmin, who partially consumed and partially sold them.

On the 19th of the same month, defendant Ma Chongyang purchased 500 grams of drugs in Xi'an City and sold them to Huang Jianmin the next day. Huang Jianmin partially sold the purchased drugs and partially hid them at his residence. At around 5:00 p.m. on the 25th, public security personnel arrested Huang Jianmin and a person named Lin, who had come to purchase drugs, at Huang's residence. They seized 19 grams of caffeine and 83.9 grams of drugs containing heroin from the residence and from Lin.

On the evening of the 20th of the same month, defendant Ma Chongyang, together with defendant Li Liang, drove to Chengdu City, Sichuan Province to purchase drugs. At around 6:00 p.m. on the 24th, Ma Chongyang purchased 21 packages of drugs in Chengdu for RMB 230,000. At around 1:00 p.m. on the 25th, Ma Chongyang and Li Liang were arrested on their way back to Xi'an. Public security personnel seized 20 packages of methamphetamine, net weight 976 grams, and one package of drugs containing methamphetamine and caffeine, net weight 82 grams, from the vehicle.

The court held that defendants Ma Chongyang and Li Liang, for the purpose of seeking illegal profits, knowingly trafficked and transported drugs, and their actions constituted the crime of drug trafficking and transportation. Defendant Huang Jianmin, for the purpose of seeking illegal profits, trafficked drugs, and his actions constituted the crime of drug trafficking. Ma Chongyang trafficked and transported a large quantity of drugs and played a major role in the joint crime as a principal offender, and he should be punished for all crimes in which he participated. Ma Chongyang had previously been subjected to re-education through labor and sentenced for theft, but he did not repent and committed the crime of drug trafficking and transportation again during the probation period of parole, demonstrating deep subjective malice and high personal danger. Huang Jianmin trafficked a large quantity of drugs. Given his good attitude in admitting guilt, he could be sentenced to death but not executed immediately. Li Liang had previously been sentenced for an intentional crime and committed another crime within five years after the completion of the sentence, constituting a recidivist and should be given a heavier punishment according to law. Given that he played a supporting role in the joint crime as an accessory, his punishment could be lenient according to law. Accordingly, Ma Chongyang was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved; Huang Jianmin was sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve; and Li Liang was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of fifteen years.

3. The Case of Defendant Huang Xianmin et al. for Drug Trafficking

Since November 2007, defendant Huang Xianmin had been selling K powder and other drugs in the urban area of Wenzhou City, Zhejiang Province, and successively employed defendants Tong Junxiang and Zhao Guojing to deliver drugs and collect payments.

In April 2008, defendant Li Qunhui sought to purchase 5 kilograms of K powder from Huang Xianmin. Huang Xianmin then contacted defendant Zhou Hao. Huang Xianmin, Li Qunhui, and Tong Junxiang met Zhou Hao in a hotel room in Wenzhou City. Huang Xianmin asked Tong Junxiang to test the K powder to confirm its quality, then purchased 6 kilograms of K powder from Zhou Hao. Subsequently, Huang Xianmin gave part of the K powder to Li Qunhui. Li Qunhui later believed that the batch of K powder was of poor quality and stored the K powder with Huang Xianmin, asking Huang to process and sell it on his behalf.

In early May of the same year, defendant Li Qunhui again called defendant Huang Xianmin to purchase 2 kilograms of high-quality K powder. Huang Xianmin again sought to purchase from defendant Zhou Hao. On May 3, Zhou Hao sold 2 kilograms of K powder to Huang Xianmin at Huang's rental residence. Huang Xianmin and Zhao Guojing sold 1 kilogram of the K powder to Li Qunhui. The next afternoon, public security personnel arrested Huang Xianmin and Zhao Guojing, seizing 2.19 grams of methamphetamine (ice) and 0.64 grams of Magu from Huang Xianmin's person, and 5.34 grams of K powder and 2.88 grams of cannabis flowers from Zhao Guojing's person. From Huang's rental residence, they seized 7,068.84 grams of K powder, 406.2 grams of methamphetamine (ice), 220.4 grams of ecstasy (MDMA), 565.69 grams of Magu, 763 grams of cannabis flowers, and 12.99 grams of cannabis seeds, among other drugs.

The court held that defendants Huang Xianmin, Zhou Hao, Li Qunhui, Tong Junxiang, and Zhao Guojing, for the purpose of seeking illegal profits, knowingly trafficked drugs, and their actions constituted the crime of drug trafficking. Huang Xianmin trafficked a large quantity and wide variety of drugs and played a major role in the joint crime, and he should be punished for all crimes in which he participated. Zhou Hao and Li Qunhui also trafficked a large quantity of drugs and should be punished according to law. Given that Li Qunhui had the meritorious performance of assisting public security organs in arresting accomplices after his arrest, his punishment could be lenient according to law. Tong Junxiang and Zhao Guojing played secondary roles in the joint crime as accessories, and their punishment could be lenient according to law. Accordingly, Huang Xianmin was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved; Zhou Hao was sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve; Li Qunhui was sentenced to life imprisonment; and both Tong Junxiang and Zhao Guojing were sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of fifteen years.

4. The Case of Defendant Guan Hui et al. for Drug Trafficking

In the summer of 2004, defendant Guan Hui purchased approximately 241.5 grams (700 pills) of ecstasy (MDMA) in Heihe City, Heilongjiang Province.

In August of the same year, defendant Guan Hui instructed defendant Zhang Shaoping to travel to Zhuhai City, Guangdong Province to purchase approximately 34.5 grams (100 pills) of ecstasy (MDMA) and approximately 113.2 grams of K powder from "A Gui" (at large). Zhang Shaoping concealed the drugs in a mooncake box and mailed them to Guan Hui's girlfriend, Chen Qi, who forwarded them to Guan Hui. Between 2004 and 2005, Guan Hui also purchased ecstasy (MDMA) from "A Gui" on four separate occasions, totaling approximately 138 grams (400 pills). "A Gui" concealed the ecstasy in a microwave oven and sent them to Guan Hui via a freight company.

In September 2006, defendant Guan Hui agreed with defendant Zeng Xianmin to purchase drugs from Zeng. At the end of the same month, at Chen Qi's residence in Aihui District, Heihe City, Zeng Xianmin sold Guan Hui approximately 200 grams of methamphetamine (ice) and approximately 145 grams (1,000 pills) of Magu.

In 2005, defendant Guan Hui agreed with defendant Li Fei to purchase drugs from Li Fei. Li Fei then ordered drugs from "Chun Ge" (at large) in Guangzhou City. "Chun Ge" concealed the drugs in sports shoes and sent them to Heihe City via a freight company. Guan Hui arranged for defendant Zhang Shaoping and others to retrieve the drugs. From October 2005 to August 2006, Guan Hui remitted a total of over RMB 800,000 to Li Fei, purchasing approximately 2,250 grams of methamphetamine (ice), approximately 1,035 grams (3,000 pills) of ecstasy (MDMA), and approximately 174 grams (1,200 pills) of Magu. In early October 2006, Guan Hui contacted Li Fei multiple times to purchase 1,000 grams of methamphetamine (ice). Li Fei ordered methamphetamine from "A Yu" (at large) in Guangzhou City. "A Yu" concealed the 1,000 grams of methamphetamine in sports shoes and sent them to Heihe City via a freight company. On the 24th of the same month, Zhang Shaoping, acting on Guan Hui's instructions, was arrested while retrieving the drugs at the Jianbo Distribution Station in Heihe City. Public security personnel seized 995 grams of methamphetamine on the spot.

In total, defendant Guan Hui purchased approximately 3,445 grams of methamphetamine (ice), approximately 1,449 grams (4,200 pills) of ecstasy (MDMA), approximately 319 grams (2,200 pills) of Magu, and approximately 113.2 grams of K powder. Guan Hui concealed the purchased drugs at the residences of defendants Zhang Shaoping and Chen Qi, packaged the drugs together with Zhang Shaoping and Chen Qi, instructed Zhang Shaoping and others to pick up and deliver the drugs, and sold the drugs at a markup.

The court held that defendants Guan Hui, Zhang Shaoping, Li Fei, Zeng Xianmin, and Chen Qi, for the purpose of seeking illegal profits, knowingly trafficked drugs, and their actions constituted the crime of drug trafficking. Guan Hui, Zhang Shaoping, and Li Fei trafficked a huge quantity of drugs, causing great social harm, and should be punished according to law. In the joint crime, Guan Hui funded the drug purchases, organized and directed multiple persons to traffic drugs, played a major role as a principal offender, and should be punished for all crimes he organized and directed. Zhang Shaoping actively participated in the drug crime as a principal offender and should be punished for all crimes in which he participated. Chen Qi played a secondary role as an accessory and could be given a mitigated punishment according to law. Accordingly, Guan Hui was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved; Zhang Shaoping and Li Fei were sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve; and Zeng Xianmin and Chen Qi were sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of fifteen years and two years, respectively.

The criminals Chen Weidong, Ma Chongyang, Huang Xianmin, and Guan Hui, who were sentenced to death and whose death penalties were approved in the above four cases, have recently been executed.
